title: Trump Says He Would Certainly Consider Military Force Against Cuba
summary: President Donald Trump tells a Salem News Channel interview that he would certainly consider military force against Cuba before leaving office. Several outlets quote the November 12, 2026 remarks, and the Clash Report carries the earliest timestamp found.
contents:
## Event

President Donald Trump says he wants to 'get Cuba done' before he leaves office and that he would 'certainly consider' using military force against the island. Hugh Hewitt put the question during a Salem News Channel interview, and several outlets quote the answer from Trump directly. Trump describes Cuba as a 'failed' nation and names Secretary of State Marco Rubio as a 'very good, talented guy for Cuba' who 'would love to do that.'

## Location and Time

The reported statement concerns Cuba as a whole, so the map point uses the Cuba country centroid rather than a city. The interview took place on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The earliest outlet timestamp located, from the Clash Report, reads 20:48 GMT, which this record stores as 2026-11-12T20:48:00Z. The point marks the subject nation only; it does not mark any planned operational location.

## Evidence

The primary evidence comes from the recorded telephone interview with Trump on Salem News Channel, which the Clash Report quotes as saying he would 'certainly consider that, yes.' Breaking the News, G1, Infobae, and The New Republic also quote the same interview. Because these outlets repeat one original remark, this record does not count them as independent corroboration. The Intel Slava Z (@intelslava) Telegram post relays the remark at 21:01:56 UTC, after the earliest outlet timestamp. No official White House transcript appeared in the sources checked during qualification.

## Allied Relevance

The stated willingness of Trump to use force against Cuba bears directly on United States and allied planning for Caribbean security, migration flows, and sanctions enforcement. Partner governments track this rhetoric because existing US fuel restrictions on the island, together with the recent US capture of Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela, form the context for the threat. The statement offers situational awareness of the publicly stated intent of an official. It describes no order, deployment, or strike.

## Confidence and Gaps

Confidence rests on direct quotations from a recorded interview that several outlets reproduce. The timestamp gives minutes only, and the broadcast itself carries no published time, so an earlier original report remains possible. The remarks express conditional intent rather than a decision or an order. Cuban officials had issued no immediate public response when the Clash Report published its account, and no later Cuban reaction appeared in the sources checked.
allied_relevance: A stated US presidential willingness to use force against Cuba informs United States and allied threat, migration, and sanctions planning.

title: Ukrainska Pravda Reports Zelensky Meets US Envoys Kushner and Witkoff at Baldonnel
summary: Ukrainska Pravda reports that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff at Casement Aerodrome in Baldonnel, west of Dublin, on 12 November 2026. The meeting followed the envoys' talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. The Irish Independent live coverage reports the same encounter.
contents:
## Event

Ukrainska Pravda reports that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met US special envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on the evening of 12 November 2026 at Casement Aerodrome in Baldonnel, west of Dublin. The meeting followed talks that the envoys held with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow earlier that day. The Irish Independent live coverage carries a headline that reports the same encounter.

## Location and Time

The reported action occurred at Casement Aerodrome in Baldonnel, County Dublin, Ireland. The geocoded point marks the aerodrome itself rather than any aircraft position. Ukrainska Pravda dates its report to 22:55 Kyiv time on 12 November 2026, which equals 20:55 UTC. The Irish Independent page shows an earlier timestamp on a rolling live feed, so this record anchors its timing on the Ukrainska Pravda publication time.

## Evidence

Ukrainska Pravda attributes its account to Suspilne, the Ukrainian public broadcaster, and it places the encounter at the Baldonnel aerodrome. The Irish Independent live page reports that Zelensky met Kushner at Baldonnell. The DD Geopolitics Telegram post repeats the meeting claim without separate sourcing. Earlier reports from The Journal, the Associated Press, RTE, and The Hill describe a planned meeting rather than a completed one. This record rests on two independent sources: the Irish Independent and Ukrainska Pravda.

## Allied Relevance

The meeting followed two days of US-brokered trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Ukrainian and Russian delegations. Kushner described the Dublin session as a debrief that would explore ideas raised in those talks. United States and allied planners can use this development to track the status of US-led efforts toward a settlement, the question of European representation at future talks, and the diplomatic sequencing around the European Political Community summit held in Dublin.

## Confidence and Gaps

Confidence rests on two outlets that report the meeting took place, one Irish and one Ukrainian. The record lacks a primary statement from the US envoys or the Ukrainian presidency that gives the exact time, duration, or outcome. Early coverage left the venue unclear, and no source in the reviewed set reports the substance of the discussions. Search did not establish whether any outlet reported the meeting before 20:28 UTC. Ukrainska Pravda cites Ukrainian public broadcast reporting, so its independence from the conflict party remains a limitation.
allied_relevance: US and allied planners can track the status of US-brokered Ukraine peace talks and the question of European representation in future negotiations.
